title: A small goal for the coming week (XC017)
summary: Paired open-ended goal-planning case: the therapist setup is identical across participants, while embedded profiles and limited earlier self-reports differ. No completed SMART plan or expected patient reply is supplied.

source.usage: Selected self-reported habits and earlier intentions inform the embedded profile. The full extract is audit-only, not a dialogue prefix or a target response to reproduce.

therapist.context: A one-to-one conversation about a small everyday goal for the coming week. No particular goal has yet been agreed.
objectives: Help the patient choose something meaningful and develop a manageable next step, building on what they already do.
materials: Verbal discussion only; no worksheet or physical task is provided.
therapist.opening_question: Let's think about a small goal for the coming week. What would you like to work on?
conversation_plan: Explore what the patient wants to work on and why it matters.

If they want to make a plan, work out enough detail to make it usable: what they will do, when, what makes it manageable, and how they could tell how it went. Follow what remains unclear rather than a fixed order.
response_guidance: Use SMART as a planning aid, not an acronym quiz or a script. Work with the goal the patient brings up, including maintaining an approach they already find useful.
completion_criteria: The patient has a next step they consider useful and manageable, or has expressed a reason to leave the plan open or stop. A fully specified goal is not required for a natural conclusion.

background.independence: Requires some assistance with basic activities

known_facts.text: I use a list beside me to keep track of what I need to do, and tick things off after finishing them.
I keep a calendar nearby and write down appointments so I do not miss them.
I like to allow more time for planning. I have described preparing a packing list well ahead of a trip to avoid a last-minute rush.
